# OnePreview

> OnePreview provides a native file-preview app for Mac, iPhone and iPad, and a separate free Markdown-to-PDF web tool. The web tool works without the app or an account.

Product facts reviewed on 2026-10-10:

- On macOS, the app extends Finder Quick Look for supported files; users can select a file and press Space after enabling the extension.
- On iPhone and iPad, users open supported files in OnePreview from Files using Open With. The app does not replace the built-in Files Quick Look preview for every normal tap.
- App preview formats include Markdown, MDX, TextBundle, TextPack, source code, plain text, logs, JSON, JSONL, YAML, XML, CSV, TSV, TOML, ENV, Apple property lists, ZIP/TAR.GZ archives, folders and SQLite databases. App preview support is not the web converter's input-format list.
- In the native OnePreview app on macOS, iPhone and iPad, standard .md and .markdown documents can also be exported as A4 PDF reports with tables, wrapped code, Mermaid diagrams and KaTeX math. Export is an action inside the app, not inside Finder Quick Look or the built-in Files preview. MDX, TextBundle and TextPack preview support does not imply PDF export support.
- Native previews use local processing and selectively cache slow rendered results. Cache reuse is conditional on document identity and rendering settings; do not claim every file is cached, a fixed speedup, or identical performance across devices and documents.
- The current web converter accepts .md and .markdown text files or pasted Markdown. It supports GitHub-style tables, code blocks, Mermaid diagrams and KaTeX-compatible math. It provides one A4 layout, page numbers, repeated table headers and code wrapping.
- Conversion runs in the browser session. Document text and explicitly selected images are not uploaded to a conversion server. Remote images are not fetched automatically. Loading the website and bundled assets still requires network access; this is not a claim of guaranteed offline operation.
- The web tool opens the browser or system Print / Save as PDF workflow. It does not directly download a PDF independently of that dialog. On iPhone and iPad, saving and sharing use the system print preview.
- Limits: 500 KB of Markdown, 100 pages, up to 16 selected images, 5 MB per image and 20 MB total. Oversized rows or content that cannot fit safely generate an error. Missing images and invalid diagrams or formulas generate notices.
- MDX components, custom scripts, TextBundle and TextPack are not supported by this first web export release.
- The current basic web tool is free. It requires neither an account nor installation of the native app. Consult the live product pages for current availability and terms.
- Known print compatibility limit: Hindi/Devanagari displays correctly in the tested preview, but macOS Chromium-generated PDF text can contain incorrect extracted characters. Verify copied text before sharing. Accurate text extraction is not guaranteed across all browsers or print destinations.

## Primary pages

- [App overview](https://one-preview.luopeike.com/): Native app capabilities and the separate web converter.
- [Markdown to PDF](https://one-preview.luopeike.com/tools/markdown-to-pdf/): Working converter, localized example, usage instructions, limits and common questions.
- [App setup and platform workflows](https://one-preview.luopeike.com/help): macOS extension setup and iPhone/iPad file-opening instructions.
- [Support](https://one-preview.luopeike.com/support): Contact and issue-reporting guidance.
- [Privacy](https://one-preview.luopeike.com/privacy-policy): Published privacy information; app diagnostics and web document processing should not be conflated.
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6760284919): Native app download and current store information.
